newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Delayed Mir cargo rocket ready for launch.
newsitem.headline: Delayed Mir cargo rocket ready for launch.

text.p: Russia, still smarting from the embarrassing loss of its Mars-96 mission at the weekend, is about to launch a cargo craft loaded with supplies for the Russian-U.S. crew on the Mir space station.
A spokesman for Russia's military space forces told Reuters the Progress M-33 rocket would lift off from Russia's Baikonur cosmodromme in Kazakhstan at 2320 GMT on Tuesday.
The mission has been delayed for more than a month, mainly due to financial problems holding up production of the Soyuz-U booster rocket.

Among 2.4 tonnes of food, water, fuel and equipment will be vital tanks and pumps designed to relieve one of the crew's most pressing problems -- damaged toilets on the ageing 10-year-old space station. The toilets are close to overflowing.
The Progress, also carrying Christmas and New Year gifts from the crew's families, should dock with Mir on November 22.

The Mir crew -- cosmonauts Valery Korzun and Alexander Koleri and U.S. astronaut John Blaha -- had been due to be relieved in mid-December. But cash problems meant the launch of the next crew, including a German, was postponed to February.
Blaha and his two Russian colleagues have been aboard Mir station since September 19.
Four Mir launches have been held up this year because of money troubles in the Russian space industry.
The unmanned Mars-96 probe, which crashed into the sea off Chile on Monday just over a day after lift-off, was launched two years late due to a lack of state funds.
Around $300 million worth of work and equipment was lost when the stricken craft failed to break out of Earth's orbit.
A faulty Proton booster is thought to have caused the crash.
But some officials have said shortage of cash for Russia's prestigious space programme was at the root of the calamity.
